Section 1.title: Short Title and Commencement: (1) This Act may be called the Domestic Violence (Offence
Section 1.content: and Punishment) Act, 2008) (2065 B.S) (2) This Act shall come into force immediately.

Section 2.title: Definitions: In this Act unless the context otherwise requires:
Section 2.content: a) “Domestic Violence” means any form of physical, mental, sexual and economic abuse perpetrated by any person to the other person with whom he has a domestic relationship. The definition also covers acts of reprimand or emotional abuse. b) “Domestic relationship” means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household and are related by consanguinity, marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family; or a dependant or domestic help living in the same family. c) “Physical abuse” means any act or conduct as per to prevailing law, which is of such nature as to cause bodily harm or injury except the losing and breaking of limbs; illegally detaining a person, inflicting physical pain or any other act connected therewith and incidental thereto. d) “Mental abuse” means any act of threatening the aggrieved person of physical torture, showing terror, reprimanding him, accusing him of false deeds, forcefully evicting him from the house or otherwise causing injury or harm to the aggrieved person emotionally and this phrase also denotes discrimination carried out on the basis of thought, religion or culture and customs and traditions. e) “Sexual abuse” means any conduct of a sexual nature that abuses, humiliates, degrades or otherwise violates the dignity of any person; or any other act that hampers safe sexual relations. f) “Economic abuse” includes deprivation of all or any property jointly or separately held by the aggrieved person to which he is entitled to under the law; or deprivation of or access to employment opportunities, economic resources or means. g) “Aggrieved person” means any person who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondents and who alleges to have been subjected to an act of domestic violence by the perpetrator. h) “Perpetrator” means the person having family relations with the aggrieved person who alleges to have been subjected to an act of domestic violence by the respondent and this word also indicates any person who is involved on some way in the act of domestic violence or in the abetment of the crime. i) “Police Office” means that Police Office close the residence of the aggrieved person, the perpetrator ! or that office which is closest to the scene of crime and the word also indicates the Women or Children Service Center under the District Police Office; or Police Post or Sub-Police Post under the Police Office. j) “Local Body” shall be understood to mean the place of residence of the aggrieved person or the perpetrator or the Village Development Committee or Municipality where the crime took place and the phrase also denotes the Ward Committee of the Municipality. k) “Court” means any court that is prescribed and notified by the Government of Nepal in the Gazette of Nepal. l) “Prescribed” or “as prescribed” means prescribed or as prescribed in the Rules made under this Act.

Section 3.title: Domestic Violence shall not be committed, aided or abetted: (1) No body shall commit; or aid
Section 3.content: or abet; or attempt or incite the commission of acts of domestic violence. (2) Whoever commits an act contrary sub-section (1) shall be deemed to have committed an offence under this Act.

Section 4.title: File complaint or petition: (1) Any person who has reason to believe that an act of domestic violence
Section 4.content: has been, or is being, or is likely to be committed, may immediately lodge a written or oral complaint with the Police Office, National Women’s Commission or Local body. (2) In pursuance to sub-section (1), a complaint shall be registered immediately if received in a written manner; and after writing down the factual details along with the signature of the complainant, if received in an oral manner. (3) If the complaint is lodged in the National Women’s Commission, necessary action will be initiated in accordance with the existing law that governs the National Women’s Commission. (4) If the complaint is lodged in the Police Station, excluding the time of travel, the perpetrator shall be produced in the Police Office within 24 hours of the lodging of the complaint for the recording of his statement and if he disobeys to be brought, force may be applied for his arrest. (5) If the complaint is lodged with the Local Body, excluding the time of travel, the perpetrator shall be produced in the Local Body within 24 hours of the lodging of the complaint for the recording of his statement and if he disobeys to be brought, force may be applied for his arrest. (6) If the aggrieved person has been physically wounded or mentally tortured as a result of the act of domestic violence, he shall be immediately sent to the nearest hospital or health post for necessary treatment and an injury report shall be drawn up. If the injury report is prepared by the Local Body, a copy of it shall be sent to the Police Station. (7) While conducting preliminary investigation on the complaint lodged as per sub-section (1) of section 4, if the situation so requires, the aggrieved person and his dependants shall be provided immediate protection with the help of the Police Office. (8) Upon statements recorded as per sub-sections (4) or (5) of section 8, if there is reason to believe that an act of domestic has been committed, and if the aggreived person so desires, the police officer or local body officer, may, within 30 days from the date of registration of the complaint, conduct reconciliation between the parties. (9) While conducting reconciliation according to sub-section (8), as per necessity and availability, assistance may be taken from a psychologist, sociologist, social activist, a family member trusted by the aggrieved person and any other witness. The psychological and social effects on the aggrieved person, of such reconciliation as well as his right to confidentiality shall be borne in mind. (10) The Police Officer or Local Body Officer shall, while conducting the prosecution and arriving at a decision upon the receipt of the complaint, keep the perpetrator on the due date of the Court. (11) If the perpetrator fails to present himself pursuant to sub-sections (4) and (5); or he cannot be made present; or the parties fail to settle their dispute through reconciliation, the Police Officer and Local body officer shall, if the complainant so consents, after the expiry of 15 days as per sub- section (8) and within 15 days after such expiry, send the complaint mentioning these details, along with evidence and other legal documents incidental thereto, to the Court. (12) It shall be the duty of the Police Officer to provide assistance as per sub-sections (5) and (7).

Section 5.title: Court shall take action: (1) Upon the receipt of a complaint as per sub-section (11) of section 4, the
Section 5.content: Court shall procecute and decide the case as per this Act, on the basis of such complaint. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), the aggrieved person may directly file his complaint with the Court.

Section 6.title: Power to grant interim protection order: (1) If the Court has reason to believe, on the basis of
Section 6.content: preliminary investigation of the complaint, that the aggrieved person needs to be given immediate protection, it may, till the time the final decision on the complaint is made, pass the following orders in the name of the perpetrator: (a) To allow the aggrieved person to continue living in the shared household, to provide him with food, clothes, to not cause physical injury to him and to behave with him in a civilized and dignified manner. (b) To provide necessary treatment or to give the required amount for the treatment of the aggrieved person if he has incurred physical or mental injury. (c) To make necessary arrangements for the separate living of the perpetrator in the event that it’s not conducive for them to live together, and in such cases, make necessary arrangements for the maintenance of the aggrieved person. (d) To not insult, threaten or behave in an uncivilized manner; or aid and abet these acts. (e) To not trouble the aggrieved person by entering his place of separate residence or harass him in public roads or enter his place of employment; or through the media or in any other way. (f) To carry out or arrange for getting carried out, necessary and relevant action for the protection and welfare of the aggrieved person. (2) On the basis of preliminary investigation upon the complaint, if the Court has reason to believe that as per sub-section (1), the minor children of the aggrieved person or any other person dependant on him, need to be given protection, the Court shall issue, from within sub-section (1), any appropriate order.

Section 7.title: Proceedings to be held in camera: (1) If the aggrieved person so requests, every proceeding and
Section 7.content: decision upon the complaint to which this Act applies, shall be held in camera. (2) In accordance with sub-section (1), during the proceedings and hearings in camera, the claimant, respondents, their respective legal practitioners and only others who have the permission of the Court, shall be allowed to enter the court room.

Section 8.title: Summary Court procedure to be followed: While conducting prosecution and deciding the case as
Section 8.content: per this Act, the procedures of the Summary (Court) Procedures Act, 2028 (1971) shall be followed.

Section 9.title: Perpetrator to bear expenses of treatment: (1) If a person who has been subject to domestic
Section 9.content: violence is injured physically or mentally so as to require medical help, his total costs of treatment in the hospital shall be borne by the perpetrator. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), if the Court has reason to believe that the perpetrator is an indigent person, it may order for the sanctioning of treatment expenses for the aggrieved person, from the Service Center as per section 11.

Section 10.title: Compensation orders: The Court may, depending on nature of the act of domestic violence, its
Section 10.content: degree, the pain undergone by the aggrieved person, and also taking into account the economic and social status of the perpetrator and aggrieved person, order the perpetrator to pay appropriate compensation to the aggrieved person.

Section 11.title: Service Centre: (1) For the immediate protection of the aggrieved person, and for the separate stay of
Section 11.content: the aggrieved person during the course of treatment, the Nepal Government, according to need, may establish Service Centers. (2) For the purpose of sub-section (1), any organization may, after taking permission as prescribed, establish and operate Service Centers. (3) Service centers operating as per sub-section (2) shall be given financial and other aid from the Fund established under section 12 of this Act. (4) The service centre shall provide, as per necessity, legal aid, psycho-social service and economic aid to the aggrieved person. (5) The provisions of management, operation and monitoring of the Service Centre shall be as prescribed.

Section 12.title: Service Fund: (1) Nepal Government shall, for the operation of Service Centers established pursuant
Section 12.content: to sub-section (1) of section 11, establish a Service Fund. (2) In the Fund established as per sub-section (1), the following funds shall be kept: (a) Funds received from the Nepal Government (b) Funds received from any national or foreign organizations, institutions or individuals (c) Funds received from any other source. (3) The management and operation of the Service Fund shall be as prescribed.

Section 13.title: Punishment: (1) Whoever commits the act of domestic violence shall be punished with a fine of three
Section 13.content: thousand rupees which may extend up to twenty-five thousand rupees; or six months of imprisonment; or both. (2) Whoever attempts to commit domestic violence or abets the crime or incites others to commit the crime shall be liable to half the punishment of that of the perpetrator. (3) Whoever has been punished once for the offence of domestic violence shall be liable to double the punishment upon every repetition of the offence. (4) If a public servant commits the offence of domestic violence, he shall be liable to an additional ten percent punishment over and above the prescribed punishment. (5) Whoever fails to obey Court orders issued according to Section 6 shall be fined two thousand rupees to fifteen thousand rupees; or four months of imprisonment; or both.

Section 14.title: Limitation Period: The complaint, for an offence committed as per this Act, shall be filed within ninety
Section 14.content: days of the commission of the crime.

Section 15.title: Case may be filed as per existing law: Nothing in this Act shall prevent the investigation, trial and
Section 15.content: decision of an offence which is punishable under this Act as well as an an existing law for the time being in force.

Section 16.title: Shall be according to existing law : This Act shall apply to the provisions under the Act and in all
Section 16.content: other cases, the existing law shall apply.

Section 17.title: Right to make Rules: The Nepal Government may make such Rules as it may deem necessary for
Section 17.content: carrying out the purposes of this Act.   Date of passage of Bill: Baishak 6, 2065 (April 19, 2009) Date of certification: Baishak 14 2065 (April 27, 2009)
